carrier_result.VERDICT: PASS - 25-way does not breach on the largest call

cost.note: this run used NO keyterm, so it billed at the 0.0043 base rate, not 0.0056. The estimate was $3.14 at the keyterm rate; actual is lower.

params_difference.note: the 2-word difference is the keyterm set, not nondeterminism. The two runs are NOT otherwise identical, which is stated rather than glossed.

limits_of_this_test: 25 requests is ONE sample of concurrency. It shows the largest call survives at 25-way; it does not characterise the latency DISTRIBUTION under sustained load.
Duration is ~24x shorter than a real run. A 25-hour sustained run at 25-way may queue differently from a 3-minute burst.
Single key only. Two-account behaviour is out of scope on contract grounds.
A PASS is evidence that 25 does not break the largest call today. It is not a capacity guarantee.
supports: TRANSCRIBE_CONCURRENCY 16 -> 25. Saves 8.7 h of a ~24 h run with zero measured downside.
